title: Performing corneal crosslinking under local anaesthesia in patients with Down syndrome

groups.description: Prospective case series: keratoconus in patients with Down syndrome treated with epithelium-off CXL under local anaesthesia following the Dresden protocol (9 mm debridement, 0.1% riboflavin with 20% dextran for 30 min, 30 min UVA with UV-X 1000; irradiance not restated); 9 eyes of 7 patients scheduled, CXL completed in 7 eyes; ages 15 to 34 years (Table 2, Results).

exclusions.what: Patient 1 OD (Tab2 R3) and patient 2 OS (Tab2 R5)
exclusions.reason: 'CXL completed: No': the procedure was aborted before UVA irradiation because the cornea stayed thinner than 400 µm; these eyes received neither cross-linking nor a ring segment and are not a declared observation group
no Kmax: Pentacam measurements unreliable, all keratometry cells printed n/a

exclusions.what: Kmax of patient 5 at 3 years and the cohort mean preoperative Kmax
exclusions.reason: given only in the Results text, not in a table cell

notes: Per-eye rows exist, so the series are individual eyes (one series per eye) and no group mean is extracted.
Two patients (1 and 4) were treated bilaterally with a 3-month interval; the two eyes of one patient are not independent.
Hypoosmolar riboflavin was added in three eyes whose thickness was below 400 µm after isotonic riboflavin; two of them were aborted and one completed CXL (which eye is not stated).
Patient 4 is listed as 15 years old in Table 2 and described as a 16-year-old in the Results text; the group is 'mixed' either way.
Visual acuity and thinnest pachymetry columns of Table 2 are not used.
